items.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: They were marvelous guitar players, you know, like Bucky Pizzarelli here

ctx.x: Did the music that you played earlier in the day, differed from the music that you played in the after hours club?

Well, yeah, because I was playing with these wonderful little groups. They were marvelous guitar players, you know, like Bucky Pizzarelli here, they were those kind of players, family players that all played in the family. Everybody in their family played guitar, but mostly Italian families. And they were brilliant players, really. They just learned, well it was handed down in the family. And I had formal training, with Carl Barladen during those days, and it was just great to fall in and be able to play with…

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: and Jack Lesberg was involved, I was, George, and then George and I really hooked up

ctx.x: No kidding. What a life, huh? You recorded some marvelous duo records, in fact I think you said some of your best things are duos?

Oh yeah. My favorite records are — the first duo I made was with Tony Mottola, then I got hooked up with George Barnes who is one of America’s great individual guitar players I ever heard, nobody played like George, and he was in the studio scene with us. And he was fed up with them, so he always had little projects going on with jazz on the weekend somewhere, and some little project where he arranged something that had a lot of body to it, and Jack Lesberg was involved, I was, George, and then George and I…
And Zoot Sims and Stephane Grappelli, all those folks.
